# Reference: output-templates.md

# Output templates

Read the template for the requested output before writing it. Use Markdown headings and tables, and offer to reformat for printing (no tables) or slides.

**Contents:** A Lesson plan · B Educator-created resource · C Learner worksheet · D Multi-session unit · E Quick starter · F Feedback on a plan · G SDG Lens plan · H Export formats · I Quiz · J Levelled text · K Sharing pack · L Learner rubric · Worked example

## Output A: Lesson Plan (Mode 2: learners create; mirrors the handbook template)
Write it in the language(s) chosen in question 13c (for a bilingual plan, put the two languages side by side or one under the other, with a glossary of key terms), and at the length the educator chose in question 13a:
- **Compact outline:** about 600 words (roughly one printed page). Keep every step below, but in short lines: one line per tier, 3–4 prompts, one debrief question per EMC² pillar used, and the 4-line Quality Check.
- **Detailed version:** about two printed pages, adding teacher notes, sample scripts or examples, fuller differentiation and needs-specific adjustments. The Quality Check stays at four lines.

```
# [Title]: [Art form] × SEL
Subject: … | Topic/Concept: … | Grade/Age: … | Duration: … | Group size: …
Use: Inductive (introduce) / Deductive (reinforce) | EMC² focus: E · M · CI · C | Curriculum link (if any): …

## Step 1: Learning objectives (integration objectives only)
Learners will be able to:
- … (2–4 do-able, observable objectives tied to the art form)
**Success criteria (share with learners):**
- I can … (subject) · I can … (art form as a way of showing understanding) · I can … (SEL)
**Materials:** … | **No-tech alternative:** …
**Educator prep (≈ __ min):** …

## Step 2: Introduction (__ min)
- Hook (e.g. show a teacher-drawn doodle / play a 60-sec soundscape / freeze a tableau)
- Concept introduction or revision, with the key facts listed

## Step 3: Activity: getting learners to doodle / use music / act (__ min)
- Modelling: …
- Instructions (numbered, learner-friendly)
- Prompts:
  - Prompt 1 (concept): …
  - Prompt 2 (feelings / perspective): …
  - Prompt 3 (metaphor / qualities): …
  - Prompt 4 (interdependence / real-world link): …
- Grouping & roles: …
- Three tiers (learners choose where possible): Support … | Core … | Stretch …
- Needs-specific adjustments: …
- Quick check during the activity: …

## Step 4: SEL integration (EMC²)
| Pillar | How learners develop it in this activity | Debrief question |
|---|---|---|
| Empathy | … | … |
| Mindfulness | … | … |
| Critical Inquiry | … | … |
| Compassion | … | … |

## Step 5: Share, reflect and close (__ min)
- Gallery walk / performance / listening circle …
- Reflection prompts / exit ticket, linked to the success criteria …
- Self- or peer assessment: two stars and a wish, using the "I can" statements
- Transfer / home connection: one no-cost way to use the idea or SEL skill outside class …
- Monitoring checklist: broad participation? engaged vs confused/hesitant? emotional reactions? → notes for next time
- ⚠️ Emotional-safety note (if relevant)

## Step 6: Share and discuss
Suggestion for sharing with colleagues or the community; licence reminder.

## ✨ Quality Check
Aligned ✔ | Fits time ✔ | EMC² goal ✔ | Success criteria ✔ | Age-appropriate ✔ | Licences checked ✔
Inclusion check: … | UDL check: …
Glows: … | Could grow by: …

Timing total: __ + __ + __ = [duration] ✔

## 📚 Sources consulted
Facts: [1] Organisation/author. (Year). Title. Link (accessed date)
Resources for class use: [2] Title, author, link, licence (TASL)

Framework adapted from Keep Calm and STEAM Ahead! … CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
⚠️ This was created with the help of AI, and AI can make mistakes. Please check facts, figures, links and licences, and adapt the plan to your learners, before using it.
```
Every other finished output (B to L) ends with the same three items: Sources consulted (if any), the framework credit and the AI disclaimer. Questions, the welcome and the brief never carry them.

## Output B: Educator-Created Resource (Mode 1)
For finished doodles (including images, where the platform can make them), original songs and chants, soundscape scripts and drama scripts, also follow `creating-doodles-music-scripts.md`.
- **Doodle:** Subject, concept and grade; 3–5 key elements; relatability device; a **step-by-step drawing guide** (basic shapes, then elements, then combine, then labels and bubbles, then a dash of colour), written so a non-artist can draw it on a board; the speech-bubble text; evaluation; 5–9 discussion questions spread across EMC²; ways learners can extend the doodle.
- **Soundtrack / soundscape cue sheet:** a table with columns `Time | Lesson moment | Sound/music type to source (or make) | Intended mood | Volume | Teacher action`; search keywords for open repositories; a DIY-sound alternative; an evaluation (ambience right? invites reflection?).
- **Script:** title; characters (with personality traits tied to **accurate** concept properties); setting; a monologue, dialogue, narration or tableau sequence, with stage directions in *(italics)*; a fact-check box mapping each line to the concept; reflection-journal prompts; staging tips for a normal classroom.

## Output C: Learner Worksheet
Learner-friendly title; a short "What you need"; a quick model or example; prompt boxes with space; a feelings or emotion word bank (age-appropriate); a self-reflection section ("What did you feel? What new idea came to mind?"); a 2-item self-check. Note in brackets where blank drawing or writing space should go.

## Output D: Multi-session Unit
A table: `Session | Focus concept | Art form | EMC² pillar | Activity | Output | Minutes`. Build up from doodle (understand), to music (feel and context), to drama (perspective and action), and finish with a learner-led showcase. Then a full Output A for session 1, and the others on request.

## Output E: Quick Starter (5–10 min)
```
⚡ [Name] | [Art form] | [minutes]
Do: (3 bullet steps)
Ask: (1–2 reflection questions, EMC²-tagged)
Needs: (materials, usually just paper/pen/voice)
```

## Output F: Feedback on an existing plan
Single-Point Rubric table with **Glows** and **Grows** per criterion, then an "Upgraded version" with the changes marked ➕.

## Output G: SDG Lens Plan (Mode 4; mirrors the Chapter 5 templates)
**G1, educator applies the SDG Lens** (a resource the educator creates):
```
# [Issue] through [Art form(s)]: SDG Lens
Step 1 · Spot the issue: Subject … | Concept … | Grade/Age … | Real-world issue …
Step 2 · Local story: whose life it touches, close to home …
Step 3 · Map the SDGs: Main SDG … | Connected SDGs …
Step 4 · Art form(s) and creation: ☐ Doodle ☐ Music/soundscape ☐ Drama
         (describe the creation: doodle guide / cue sheet / script)
Step 5 · Build EMC²
  Check: accurate? ☐ | connects to learners' lives? ☐ | reflective without undue distress? ☐ | points to hope or action? ☐
  | Empathy | Mindfulness | Critical Inquiry | Compassion |  (one question each)
Step 6 · Act and share: use as ☐ intro ☐ review ☐ discussion prompt ☐ call to action
  One action learners will take: … | Who they will share it with: …
```
**G2, learners take creative action** (lesson plan): the Output A structure with these changes:
- Header adds **SDG(s)**.
- Step 2 introduction **starts from learners' own lives** (a local change, a news story, a memory, a person they know).
- Step 3 lets learners **choose** an art form (some prefer to doodle rather than perform).
- Step 4 names the SEL integration **and one concrete action**.
- Step 5 adds "Does it balance honesty about the issue with hope and agency?" and monitors "engaged, or anxious and withdrawn? Did it end on a hopeful note?"
- Step 6 suggests sharing beyond the classroom (assembly, parents, panchayat or municipal council).
- Include an **age-adaptation** box (5–8 / 8–11 / 14–18) and a **"Swap the issue"** line showing how the same plan works for another SDG.

## Output H: Export formats
On request, re-present any output as:
- **Printable:** no tables wider than the page, clear headings, blank space marked for drawing or writing, black-and-white friendly.
- **Slide outline:** one slide per lesson phase, with a title, 3–5 bullet points, a speaker note and a suggestion for an image or doodle (with a licence note if it's not the educator's own).
- **Word / Google Docs:** clean headings and tables that paste well; suggest "File › Download" to save as .docx or PDF.
- **WhatsApp / SMS (low bandwidth):** plain text only, no tables, short lines, emojis as section markers, under about 1,500 characters per message, split into numbered messages if needed. Keep the credit and AI disclaimer in the last message.
You can't create files yourself unless your platform allows it; if not, give the formatted text for the educator to copy.

## Output I: Starter or exit quiz
3–6 questions matched to the success criteria and learner stage: a mix of multiple-choice, true/false-with-reason and one open question linked to the art activity ("Point to / describe the part of your doodle that shows…"). Give an **answer key** and, for each wrong option, the **likely misconception** and a one-line fix. For early years, use pictures, gestures or oral questions instead.

## Output J: Level a text
Take a passage (the educator's own, or one you write) and rewrite it at **2–3 reading levels** (e.g. early reader, core, advanced). Keep the same facts and key vocabulary in every version, with a short glossary for the simplest level. Only level text the educator owns or that is openly licensed for adaptation (see `research-and-licensing.md`); never level a text marked ND or all rights reserved.

## Output K: Prepare for sharing as an open resource
The handbook invites educators to share their creations with the community. Produce a sharing pack:
- **Title** and a **2–3 sentence description** (topic, learner stage, art form, SEL focus, SDG if any).
- **Licence label:** CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with the link, because it adapts the handbook.
- **Credits:** the educator as author; the handbook; this skill, using the line *"Created with the STEAM-SEL Lesson Designer skill by NMG (2026), created under the mentorship of EO as part of the OE4BW 2026 programme, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Source: https://github.com/nmg-002/steam-sel-lesson-designer"*; TASL credits for every third-party resource; an AI-assistance note.
- **Keywords** (subject, stage, art form, EMC², SDG) and **what's included** (plan, worksheet, script, cue sheet).
- **A check before sharing:** no learner names, faces or personal data; all third-party resources licensed for sharing; facts verified.
Remind the educator they can share it with the handbook's community repository, if one is available to them.

## Output L: Learner rubric
A 3-level table (*Getting there · Got it · Going further*) with one row each for: the subject concept; using the art form to show understanding (not artistic skill); SEL reflection; and, if relevant, working with others. Write each cell as a learner-friendly description. For ages 5–8, use faces or pictures and 2–3 rows only.

## Worked example (for calibration; adapt, don't copy)

**Brief:** Grade 5, 32 learners, rural school, Konkani/English, two learners with low vision, no internet, 40 min, Science: Germination (new concept), learners create, groups of 4.
**Recommendation:** Doodling. Germination is a staged process with interacting factors, and personifying the seed builds empathy and an understanding of perseverance. For the low-vision learners: thick black markers, large paper, tactile seed samples, and a "describer" role in their group.
**Excerpt of Step 3 prompts:**
1. Doodle water, sunlight and soil as characters talking to the seed. What does each one say?
2. Draw the seed's feelings at each stage: sleepy, determined, triumphant.
3. What qualities does the seed show? Is it a warrior breaking its shell, or a dancer reaching for the sun?
4. Show how sun, soil and water support the sapling. Add one helper (a pebble?) the seed asks for support.
**EMC²:** Empathy (the seed's struggle), Mindfulness (slow, close observation of the stages), Critical Inquiry (why do some seeds sprout faster?), Compassion (parallels with people facing challenges).
**Timing:** 5 hook (teacher doodle) + 8 concept + 5 modelling + 14 group doodling + 8 gallery walk and debrief = 40 ✔

---

# Reference: creating-doodles-music-scripts.md

# Creating doodles, music, soundscapes and scripts

Read this when the educator wants a finished creative resource rather than a plan: a doodle to show the class, a song or chant, a soundscape, or a script. Everything here follows the handbook: simple, low-cost, no artistic skill needed, accurate content, and room for learners to make their own versions.

**Contents:** 1. Doodles · 2. Songs, chants and rhythms · 3. Soundscape scripts · 4. Drama scripts · 5. Using other tools and existing resources · 6. Credits for created resources

## 1. Doodles

**Always give a drawing guide first**, so any educator can draw it on a board: basic shapes → elements → combine → labels and speech bubbles → a dash of colour (see Output B in `output-templates.md`).

**If your platform can create images**, offer to draw the doodle as well. Keep to the handbook's doodle style:
- simple black lines on a white background, a little colour for emphasis, no photorealism;
- personified elements with clear faces and feelings, short speech or thought bubbles, arrows and labels (for example the leaf as a chef, the "gas gang" in the Greenhouse Party, Auntie Mangrove);
- labels spelled correctly in the chosen output language, and scientifically accurate details (check proportions, order of stages, chemical formulas);
- age-appropriate, with diverse, non-stereotyped characters.

**Directly under every image, always add this "image card"**, in the same answer, without waiting to be asked. Testing showed these three lines are easy to forget, and they matter for accessibility, accuracy and honesty:
```
🖼️ Image card
Description: [2–4 sentences describing the doodle for learners who can't see it, as the handbook describes its own doodles]
Fact check: [confirm the labels and science are correct, or list anything to fix; AI images often misspell labels or get details wrong]
AI-generated doodle, created with [tool name, if known]. Shared under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 where the tool's terms allow.
```
Ask the image tool for the handbook's simple doodle style (black lines, a little colour, white background), not a polished illustration.

**If your platform can't create images**, give the drawing guide plus a short, ready-to-paste **image prompt** the educator can use in an image tool, for example: *"Simple hand-drawn doodle, black ink with soft green and yellow, white background: a smiling leaf wearing a chef's hat stirring a pot labelled CO₂ + H₂O, a cheerful sun saying 'Here's some energy!', a sugar cube character labelled glucose, and O₂ bubbles floating up. Clear printed labels, no other text."* Remind them to check the tool's licence terms (section 5).

**Learners first.** A teacher-made doodle is a model or a hook. The handbook's goal is learners making their own, so always pair it with learner doodle prompts.

## 2. Songs, chants and rhythms

You may write **original** songs, chants, rhymes, raps or verses about the concept. Never reproduce or adapt copyrighted lyrics; you may only *suggest* a copyrighted song, labelled as such (see `research-and-licensing.md`).

For each song, include **all** of the following in your **first answer**, not as later options. Testing showed that without this, the melody and rhythm get left out:
- **Lyrics:** 2–4 short verses and a chorus, accurate content, age-appropriate vocabulary, in the output language chosen in question 13c. Mark key subject terms in bold.
- **A simple melody** that teachers can sing without reading staff notation. Use **sargam** (Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Sa) where it fits the context, or doh-re-mi, one syllable per note, with dashes for held notes, for example `Sa Re Ga – | Ga Re Sa – |`. Keep to five or six notes and a small range so everyone can sing it.
- **Or a familiar open tune:** you may suggest singing the words to a **traditional or public-domain** tune. Ask the educator to verify that the tune is genuinely traditional or public domain in their country, and never use a copyrighted pop or film melody.
- **Body percussion:** a 4-beat rhythm pattern for learners without instruments, for example `Clap · Clap · Snap · Stamp`, and a way to layer it (one group claps, one group sings).
- **Everyday-object instruments:** suggest a water xylophone, bottle shakers, desk drumming or seed rattles, as in the handbook.
- **SEL link:** one EMC² question about the song (for example "How did singing it together feel?").
- **Learner version:** invite learners to write their own verse, as in the handbook's "rewrite a verse" activity.
- **Science check of the lyrics:** song imagery must not teach a misconception. For example, water vapour is invisible, so don't describe rising vapour as "little clouds"; clouds form only when vapour condenses into droplets. Fix any line that bends the facts, or add a one-line note for the teacher.

For **data sonification**, give the data table, the note each value maps to (higher value = higher note), and how to play it on a water xylophone, sargam or a free online keyboard. Use real data only from a source you opened, or mark it "(please verify)".

## 3. Soundscape scripts

A soundscape script is a timed "sound score" that learners perform live with voices, bodies and objects, like the handbook's thunder-and-footsteps storytelling track or the Monsoon Then and Now soundscape.

Write it as a table:

| Time | Sound | How to make it | Who | Volume |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Light rain | Fingertips tapping desks, slowly building | Group A | Soft, growing |
| 0:20–0:30 | Thunder | Shaking a sheet of chart paper | One volunteer | Loud |
| … | … | … | … | … |

Then add:
- the **mood arc** (for example calm → tension → calm) and what it shows about the concept;
- a **narration line** or two to read over it, if useful;
- a **mindfulness moment:** eyes closed, listen again, "What do you notice now?";
- options for learners with hearing impairments (visual cues, vibration, a conductor's gestures) and for learners who prefer not to perform (conductor, timekeeper, recorder).

If the educator wants recorded sounds, propose **openly licensed sound libraries first** (for example Wikimedia Commons, Internet Archive, Freesound, Free Music Archive), with the licence of each sound.

## 4. Drama scripts

Write complete, original scripts as in Output B (`output-templates.md`): monologue, dialogue, narration or a tableau sequence, with stage directions in *(italics)*, characters whose traits match **accurate** properties of the concept, a fact-check box, staging tips for an ordinary classroom, and reflection-journal prompts. Also:
- give an **approximate performance time**;
- offer **roles for learners who don't want to act** (narrator, sound effects, director, prop maker);
- keep sensitive topics fictional or third-person, with opt-outs (see the guardrails in `SKILL.md`);
- for historical or real people, keep facts accurate and mark invented dialogue as imagined.

## 5. Using other tools and existing resources

- **Open resources first:** when suggesting existing images, music, sounds or videos, follow the OER-first order in `research-and-licensing.md`: openly licensed (Creative Commons) resources first, public domain next with a request to verify its status and authenticity, and copyrighted material only as a clearly labelled suggestion that the educator must check for access and accessibility.
- **AI image or music tools:** if the educator wants an AI tool to make an image or a recording, give them a clear prompt and remind them to **read the tool's licence and terms first**. Some tools restrict how their output can be shared or used, and that matters because materials shared from this skill should carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Suggest checking that the output doesn't imitate a recognisable artist, song or copyrighted character.
- **Never** claim a resource is free, open or public domain unless you saw its licence.

## 6. Credits for created resources

Add to the end of every created doodle, song, soundscape or script:
- **What it is and who made it:** for example *"Original song created with AI assistance using the STEAM-SEL Lesson Designer skill"* or *"AI-generated doodle (image created with [tool name, if known])"*.
- **Licence:** *"Shared under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, where the AI tool's terms allow."*
- **TASL credits** for any open or public-domain resources reused, and *"© Copyrighted, suggestion only"* labels for any copyrighted resources mentioned.
- The usual handbook credit and AI disclaimer (see `SKILL.md`, section 7).
